The present (1926-6) issue of the CHINA YEAR BOOK is again considerably larger than any of its predecessors. The Chapters on "Mines and Minerals," "Education," "Products," "Labour," "Opium," "Commerce," "Shipping," "Currency," etc., have been rewritten and brought up to date. The Report of the Shanghai Child Labour Commission is reprinted in full in the Chapter in "Labour." "The Political Summary" describes events up to the end of March, 1925. The Chapter on "Defence appears at the end of the Book. New Chapters include a Summary of Medical Events." "Political Parties," "Taxation" a "Bibliography for 1924," and a documented Chapter on "China's Constitutions and Election Laws." THE TERMS OF THE GOLD FRANC SETTLEMENT ARE INCLUDED IN AN APPENDIX.

With reference to the offer of new shares dated the 10th June, 1925 (made to existing shareholders of the Company) by the terms of which the sum of $30 per share was to be paid on or before the 15th July, 1925, and the sum of $30 per share on or before the 15th October, 1925, the Directors have decided that as regards those shareholders (having a registered address in the Far East) who do not feel themselves (owing to present circumstances) in a position to accept the Company's offer on or before the 15th July, 1925, a further opportunity shall be given to them to take up the new shares.

Such shareholders may accordingly take up the new shares on or before the 15th day of September before the 15th day of September, 1925, and may pay the first instalment of $30 per new share on or before that date. They will, however, be required to pay interest at 6 per cent. per annum on the amount of such first instalment from the 15th day of July, 1925, until the date of payment.

The British steamer Egrmont Castle, of the Dodwell Castle Line, which went aground last week on Tub Butahu reef in the Sulu Sea, slipped off the reef in a squall and sunk in a thousand fathoms on Sunday morning.

The crew of fifty were saved by the Coastguard cutter Corregidor and now are on their way to Manila. A valuable cargo of sugar was lost. The automatic light on the reef was unlit when the vessel grounded.

The Coastguard, utter Corregidor has arrived with 12 white and 86 Chinese, comprising the entire crew of the Egremonv Castle. They state the ship was slipping off the reef but had not yet sink when they left the scene. They believe, however, she is lost. They declared that the transfer from the vessel was made with difficulty owing to high seas and heavy wind.
[Messrs. Dodwell] and Co., Ltd. agents here for the Castle Line have received confirmatory advice.

A communiqué from Morocco says that a French aeroplane traversed Quilates, in the Spanish zone, while Spanish aeroplanes bombed enemy concentrations advancing on the French front near Hashuegan. The French and Spanish air forces have thus begun to exercise the right to fly over each other's territory, as agreed at Madrid.
It is reported from Fez that signs of lossitude have appeared amongst many Riff tribes, several of whom are demanding a cessation of hostilities.

The death is announced of Dr. Stafford Moritz Cox (Major R.A.M.C.), M.D., L.R.C.S., L.R.C.P.I., which occurred on July 24, at the General Hospital, Shanghai, in his 60th year. Dr. Cox, who was a native of Kerry, Ireland, had been ill for the past three or four years, but lately had shown great improvement, and his death came as a great surprise.
The Tatung, the first British passenger ship to reach Hankow from Shanghai since the strike, reports no molestation en route. Coolies were working at all ports.
The General Union of Labour, Commerce and Education which was closed on July 23, was allowed to be re-opened this afternoon.

According to Chinese reports, ex-President Tsao Kun, who has been a prisoner since Peng Yu-hsiang's coup d'etat, attempted to escape on July 24, disguised as a common soldier, with his moustache shaved off, but the sentry recognised him and called assistance and Tsao Kun was led back into captivity.

"I had never seen a play before, but I took my courage in both hands and went to see three of London's most widely-advertised dramas," said the Rev. Dr. J. S. Holden, M.A., preaching at St. Paul's Church, Portman-Square. "If these plays are a fair sample of those at present being served in the theatre," he continued, "we are simply mad to allow it. They are as dangerous as an open drain, a grinning menace to the nation's moral wellbeing and prosperity.
“What hidden hand is protecting those carrion dramatists who have disguised dirt with smart double entendre? Why doesn't the censor act?
"I indict him for a grave dereliction of duty, and demand his examination and dismissal."
